title: Impact of 15-month Wait-out Period on Private Property Downgraders
what_it_is: Impact of 15-month Wait-out Period on Private Property Downgraders

sections.label: HDB resale cooling measures questions
sections.summary: Questions ask how many Singaporeans the 15-month wait-out period affects, what help urgent cases get, and how the measures cool the market.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam
sentences.text: asked the Minister for National Development with the recent announcement of further cooling measures for the property sector (a) how many Singaporeans are estimated to be affected by the 15-month wait-out period for a resale HDB flat; (b) what assistance may be provided to those who are caught out by circumstances but may genuinely require housing urgently; and (c) how will the new measures cool the property market.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin
sentences.text: asked the Minister for National Development (a) for the past three years, what has been the number of HDB resale flat transactions involving buyers who are private property owners (PPOs) or PPOs who have disposed of a private property prior to submitting an application to buy a HDB resale flat; and (b) of such buyers, what is the percentage of purchasers who paid cash over valuation and who are above 55 years old.

sections.label: HDB September 2022 measures
sections.summary: On 29 September 2022, HDB announced measures to encourage financial prudence in home loans and moderate HDB resale market demand.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: On 29 September 2022, HDB announced further measures to, first, encourage home buyers to exercise greater financial prudence when taking home loans, as higher interest rates were expected over the medium term; and second, to moderate demand in the HDB resale market.

sections.label: 15-month wait-out period purpose
sections.summary: The 15-month wait-out period is a temporary measure to moderate resale flat demand and prioritise affordable public housing for those with urgent needs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: The 15-month wait-out period is a temporary measure to moderate demand for resale flats and help to prioritise access to affordable public housing for Singaporeans with more urgent housing needs, such as first-time home buyers.

sections.label: Private property owners buying resale flats
sections.summary: The number of private property owners buying HDB resale flats doubled in 2021 and the first three quarters of this year, compared to 2019 and 2020.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: The number of private property owners buying HDB resale flats has doubled in 2021 and the first three quarters of this year, compared to 2019 and 2020.

sections.label: Government Land Sale supply plans
sections.summary: The Government will consider economic and market conditions in planning half-yearly GLS supply, having raised private housing supply 75% from about 3,600 units in 2021 to around 6,300 in 2022.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: We will, however, consider the prevailing economic and market conditions, including the impact of the 15-month wait-out period, as we plan our half-yearly Government Land Sale (GLS) supply for private housing.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: We have already increased the supply of private housing on the confirmed list of the GLS programme by 75%, from about 3,600 units in 2021, to around 6,300 units in 2022.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: We are prepared to increase the GLS supply further if needed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: The Government will continue to monitor the housing market conditions and act decisively, but also carefully, to ensure the stability of the wider Singapore property market and to keep public housing inclusive, affordable and accessible to Singaporeans.

sections.label: BTO and GLS supply, loan floors
sections.summary: The Government ramped up BTO and private housing supply by some 75%, and MAS and HDB took macroprudential measures including a 3% floor for HDB loans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: As I have said earlier, the Government has also ramped up the supply of new BTO flats and increased the supply of private housing on both the confirmed list as well as the GLS programme by some 75%, from 3,600 units last year to 6,300 this year, and we will continue to see whether we may need to make some adjustments if needed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: With the concern or the potential for higher interest rates in the medium term, MAS and HDB, therefore, took precautionary measures of a macroprudential nature by increasing, for MAS, the private financial institution rate floor ceiling for the taking of housing loans for residential housing and for HDB to institute a 3% floor for HDB loans.

sections.label: HDB interest rate
sections.summary: The HDB interest rate remains at 2.6%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: For HDB, the interest rate remains at 2.6%.

sections.label: Financial help from HDB
sections.summary: Financially affected Singaporeans can approach HDB, with one option for seniors and one for any Singaporeans with extenuating circumstances, regardless of age.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: Indeed, this group of Singaporeans who are affected financially can approach HDB.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: One would be for seniors, the other would be for any Singaporeans with extenuating circumstances, regardless of age.
